question: How do our dispute trends compare to CFPB complaint volume for the same period?
text:
Our disputes follow a regular seasonal pattern, but CFPB complaint volume doesn't move with it. I compared the two month by month from Jul 2024 to Jun 2026.

**Our disputes**
- There are 362 disputes in every month except Nov–Jan, when there are 574 (about 59% more). That held in both years.
- Disputed dollars follow the same pattern: about $0.20–0.24M in a normal month and about $0.34–0.36M in Nov–Jan. The highest was Dec 2025 at $0.36M.
- Win rate (won ÷ resolved) has no seasonal pattern. It ranges from 43.1% (Oct 2025) to 52.7% (Feb 2025).

**CFPB complaints (one benchmark figure per month)**
- Volume ranges from 4,135 (Sep 2025) to 6,091 (Dec 2024) and goes up and down from month to month without a clear direction.
- In 2024–25, complaints did rise during our peak season: 5,271 in Nov, 6,091 in Dec and 5,563 in Jan.
- In 2025–26 they didn't: 5,076 in Nov, 4,955 in Dec and 5,298 in Jan, which is about the same as, or below, months like Feb 2026 (5,402) and May 2026 (5,486).

**What this means**
- Our holiday-season jump looks like it comes from our own business, not from consumer complaints rising across the market. The benchmark showed a matching rise in one of the two seasons only.
- Month-to-month changes in CFPB volume (for example, 5,486 in May 2026 falling to 4,213 in Jun 2026) didn't show up in our dispute counts at all.
- **Check before relying on the counts:** having exactly 362 disputes in every regular month and exactly 574 in every peak month is unusually uniform. The dispute data may be modeled or templated rather than actual counts, so confirm its source before drawing firm conclusions from the comparison.

tables.title: Monthly Disputes, Dispute $, Win Rate vs CFPB Complaints (Jul 2024–Jun 2026)

sql: SELECT month_end, SUM(dispute_count) AS total_disputes, SUM(total_dispute_amount) AS dispute_usd, SUM(won_count)/NULLIF(SUM(resolved_count),0) AS win_rate, MAX(cfpb_complaint_count) AS cfpb_complaints, MAX(cfpb_complaint_count)-MIN(cfpb_complaint_count) AS cfpb_spread FROM __d GROUP BY month_end ORDER BY month_end
